📖 Core Definitions

Essential Terminology & Concepts

Abundance Of Digitized Text Key Concept

The amount of digitized text has grown exponentially over the past decades.

Pattern-Matching Algorithms Key Concept

Pattern matching is fundamental to text processing - finding all occurrences of a pattern string P within a text string T.

Dynamic Programming Key Concept

Dynamic programming is particularly useful for text processing problems involving sequence alignment, edit distance, and longest common subsequences.

Tries Key Concept

A trie (prefix tree) is a specialized tree data structure for storing strings, enabling efficient prefix-based operations.

📌 Key Takeaways

Section-by-Section Study Breakdown

13.2 Abundance of Digitized Text

  • The amount of digitized text has grown exponentially over the past decades.
  • Just as humans use different alphabets (Latin, Cyrillic, Chinese), computers use different encoding schemes to represent text.
  • The Fundamental Problem: Computers only understand numbers (0s and 1s), but humans work with letters, symbols, and characters.
  • We need a systematic way to convert between human text and computer numbers.

13.3 Pattern-Matching Algorithms

  • Pattern matching is fundamental to text processing - finding all occurrences of a pattern string P within a text string T.
  • Start at the beginning: Place your finger at the first character of the text 2.
  • Try to match: Compare each character of the pattern with the text starting from your current position 3.
  • If all characters match: You found the pattern!

13.4 Dynamic Programming

  • Dynamic programming is particularly useful for text processing problems involving sequence alignment, edit distance, and longest common subsequences.
  • EDIT DISTANCE (LEVENSHTEIN DISTANCE) The edit distance between two strings is the minimum number of operations (insert, delete, substitute) needed to transform one string into another.
  • Substitute: Replace one character with another The Dynamic Programming Approach: 1.
  • Fill base cases: The first row and column represent the cost of transforming from/to an empty string (just insertions or deletions) 3.

13.5 Text Compression and the Greedy Method

  • Text compression reduces storage space and transmission time.
  • Greedy algorithms like Huffman coding provide optimal prefix-free codes.
  • Huffman coding assigns shorter codes to more frequent characters.

13.6 Tries

  • A trie (prefix tree) is a specialized tree data structure for storing strings, enabling efficient prefix-based operations.
